key_drivers: Sector-wide AI-infrastructure de-rating: CORZ -26% in a month, -23.8% over 20d into the print
Beta 5.5 and 86% realised vol; two-sided fat tail, not a directional edge
Last two earnings reactions negative (-9.2%, -7.2%) after a run of positives
Operating leverage story intact per 07-20 coverage: revenue +45% YoY to $115.2M, high-density colo 9x YoY
Thin corpus: 4 usable articles, only one substantive, no filings read
what_would_change_my_mind: Evidence that the July drawdown was company-specific (contract loss, financing) rather than sector beta would shift this decisively down.
reasoning: Deeply oversold high-beta AI-infra name into a print. The one substantive article frames July as a sector de-rating with no CORZ-specific catalyst and puts CORZ on the better side of the fundamental split. That cuts both ways: an oversold bounce on a decent print is as likely as continuation. Recent reaction history has turned negative, giving a small down tilt only. Size the move large, direction near coin-flip.

key_drivers: Sleepy PA/OH community bank: 20.3% realised vol, 724k ADV, historical earnings moves clustered under 2%
Sitting exactly at the 52-week high with +5.3% 20d and +1.9% 5d run-up
Confirmed amc release 2026-07-28, call 07-29; no preview content of any kind in the corpus
Zero company-specific news: the only two usable articles are a scheduling notice and an editor's link roundup
Anchor 'earnings' dates match 10-Q filings, not releases, so the 0.74% median understates true reaction size
what_would_change_my_mind: Any read on credit trends or NIM guidance — a reserve build or a commercial credit surprise is the one thing that moves a bank this size more than 3%.
reasoning: No informational edge exists here. The corpus contains one press release announcing the call and one Seeking Alpha roundup that mentions nothing. Price is at highs with mild positive drift, which is weakly favourable but also raises the bar. Small regional banks print in line far more often than not. The confident part of this call is the magnitude, not the sign: roughly a 2% absolute move, direction essentially random.

key_drivers: At the 52-week high with the entire 20d gain (+5.6%) coming in the last five sessions — a hot run straight into the print
Spot $64.09 sits essentially on the sell-side consensus target of $64.23; limited room without a raise
Reaction skew is negative: 5 of last 8 down, median signed move about -1%, last print -3.17%
Fundamentals are fine, not a surprise: Q1 beat $0.70 vs $0.64, +140bp margin, ~$1.8bn buyback since spin, guide 'upper half' of $2.90-3.00 — already public
Corpus is 83% tier-3 and mostly generic aggregator content; no real preview
what_would_change_my_mind: A guidance raise above the $3.00 top end, or an M&A/capital-return announcement alongside the print, would flip this.
reasoning: Clean post-spin compounder with a well-telegraphed beat-and-buyback story that the market has just re-rated into highs in one week. Everything I can read about the setup is already in the price, including a guide the CEO pre-announced as trending to the upper half. FTV's reaction history is negatively skewed, and industrials that gap to 52-week highs the week before a print frequently sell the news. Modest conviction, ordinary magnitude.

key_drivers: Tebapivat sickle-cell Phase 2 failed differentiation and was discontinued 07-21; stock fell ~7% that day and is -23% from highs
That setback is pipeline, not commercial — it is already in the price and does not read through to a Q2 revenue print
The real catalyst is the mitapivat sNDA in SCD, Priority Review, PDUFA 2026-11-01, not this report
Reaction history mildly positive: +13.1% last quarter, 3 of last 4 up
73.7% realised vol on a 1.1m-share ADV means an ordinary session is already ~4.5%
what_would_change_my_mind: A PYRUKYND revenue miss or slowing launch metrics, or any hint of an FDA information request delaying the November PDUFA, makes this clearly down.
reasoning: Q2 for a commercial-stage biopharma is a revenue and burn update; the binary that matters sits in November. The July setback has de-rated the stock on a program that was never the core value driver, and last quarter's +13% suggests the launch curve was surprising to the upside. That argues a small positive tilt into an oversold print, but with only one usable article I have no read on the actual quarter. Wide distribution, near-flat direction.

key_drivers: Down 12.75% in five sessions and 22% in 20 days into the print, entirely on sector beta: PWR was sold -5.1% alongside VRT -6.7% and GEV -4.6% in a data-center-buildout unwind, with no company-specific news
Nasdaq 100 in correction on a China memory-competition scare; the de-rating is a positioning event, not a Quanta event
Consensus is on the tape and modest: $3.31 EPS on $8.59bn revenue, against a backlog-driven business with multi-year visibility
Strong recent beat cadence: +15.78%, +6.68%, +1.15% on the last three prints
Cross-current: Fed meeting with ~35% odds of a hike and 10y at 4.60% — hostile tape for long-duration capex names, and the same week punished in-line guides (GLW -15.7%, SANM -18.9%)
what_would_change_my_mind: Any commentary trimming data-center or renewables backlog conversion, or a guide merely reaffirmed rather than raised, would be enough to extend the slide in this tape.
reasoning: The two most recent articles establish that PWR's 22% drawdown is sympathy selling inside an AI-hardware unwind, not a deterioration in grid and utility capex. Positioning is washed out, expectations are explicit and unremarkable, and the company has beaten and gapped up on three of its last four prints. Against that, the tape was savagely punishing in-line guides that week, which caps conviction. Lean up, large expected magnitude either way.
